subject: Galapagos racer snake
title: A Beach Full of Snakes Waits All Year for Baby Iguanas to Hatch

scenes.text: On one Galapagos beach, snakes wait for a birth.
Marine iguanas hatch on the shore of Fernandina Island, then have to dash for the rocks above.
Galapagos racer snakes, up to four feet long, are already there. This is their best meal of the year.
Their eyes are tuned to movement. Anything that runs gets chased.
It looks like a pack. It isn't. Every snake is racing the others for the same baby.
The winner may not eat again for weeks. So nobody holds back.

description:
On Fernandina Island in the Galapagos, racer snakes gather where marine iguanas hatch.
The Galapagos racer is a slim, mildly venomous snake that grows to about 120 centimeters. Hatching season is its best feeding opportunity of the year, and its eyesight is built to pick up movement, so a hatchling running for the rocks sets off a chase. Biologists point out that the famous Planet Earth II scene is not a coordinated pack hunt: it is many snakes acting alone and competing for the same prey, and a snake that has eaten may not feed again for several weeks.
Would you run or freeze? Comment below.
first_comment: In the filmed chase, the hatchling slipped out of the coils and reached the rocks. Would you run or freeze?
